description: Create the plugins/ folder and build all SIX Tier-1 Suno Studio audio-effect plugins as JSON files with embedded JS DSP, each in its own subfolder plugins/<name>/<name>.plugin.json. These are Suno Studio (in-app effects/mixing) plugins applied to rendered audio, NOT lyric tags. Every plugin uses ONLY the confirmed g.* primitives. This is a self-contained unit; docs come in FEAT-002/FEAT-003.
steps: Create directory plugins/ with six subfolders: plugins/intimate-proximity/, plugins/de-esser/, plugins/vintage-lofi-voicer/, plugins/digital-degrade/, plugins/telephone-radio-band/, plugins/vocal-drive-edge/.

PLUGIN FORMAT (authoritative, reverse-engineered from the ONE known example — match field names/shapes exactly). Each file is a single JSON object with TOP LEVEL keys: id (string, e.g. 'intimate-proximity'), kind ('effect'), displayName (string), description (string), ports { audioIn: {kind:'audio'}, audioOut: {kind:'audio'}, extraInputs: [], extraOutputs: [] }, parameters (array), source { lang:'js', metadata:{...}, code:'<js string>' }, ui { compact: {...} }.

PARAMETERS[] shape: each parameter object has name (string, e.g. 'air'), label (string), and EITHER a continuous form { range:{min,max,step}, scale:'linear'|'log', default:<num>, unit:'db'|'ms'|'percent'|'hz' } OR a toggle/enum form { enumOptions:[{value,label},...], default:<value> }. Every plugin MUST include: a 'bypass' toggle parameter (enumOptions off/on, default off), an 'input gain' (unit db) and 'output gain' (unit db) parameter, and a 'dry/wet mix' (unit percent) parameter where mixing is meaningful (all six except where noted).

SOURCE.METADATA shape: mirror displayName, kind, description; include a 'controls' map keyed by parameter name where each entry has widget {type:'knob'|'toggle', pan:true optional}, description (string), and mirrors range/scale/unit/label/default (for knobs) or enumOptions/label/default (for toggles); include a 'ui' object with a 'compact' layout that matches the top-level ui.compact.

SOURCE.CODE shape: a JS function string 'function build(g, config) { ... }'. Read audio via g.input('audioInL') and g.input('audioInR'); read params via g.input('<param name>'); write outputs via g.output('audioOutL', <node>) and g.output('audioOutR', <node>). Use config.sampleRate where a filter/envelope needs it. START each code string with a header comment (// lines) explaining the full signal chain in order. Implement bypass by using g.lerp on the bypass control (or g.compareLt) to select between the dry input and the processed signal. Convert dB gains with g.dbToLin. End EVERY plugin with a g.tanh output-safety stage before g.output (soft-clip the final signal).

CONFIRMED PRIMITIVES — USE ONLY THESE, do not invent others: g.input, g.output, g.zero, g.constant, g.mul, g.add, g.sub, g.div, g.abs, g.max, g.min, g.clamp, g.lerp(mask,a,b), g.compareLt(a,b), g.dbToLin, g.tanh, g.biquad({input,cutoff,resonance,mode:'highpass'|'lowpass'|'peaking'|'lowshelf'|'highshelf'}), g.asymmetricOnePole({target,attackCoef,releaseCoef}). NO delay lines, reverb, noise, LFO/oscillator, or FFT. If a plugin idea would need an unconfirmed primitive, approximate it with the confirmed set and DOCUMENT the approximation in the code header comment.

PLUGIN 1 — plugins/intimate-proximity/intimate-proximity.plugin.json (id 'intimate-proximity', displayName 'Intimate Proximity'). Close-mic 'in your ear' vocal. Chain: input trim (dbToLin) -> high-shelf 'air' lift via g.biquad mode 'highshelf' cutoff ~8-12kHz (param 'air' in db) -> gentle low-mid warmth via g.biquad mode 'lowshelf' or 'peaking' ~200-400Hz (param 'warmth' in db) -> light presence bump via g.biquad 'peaking' ~3-5kHz (param 'presence' in db) -> dry/wet mix (g.lerp) -> output gain -> tanh safety. Params: input gain (db), air (db), warmth (db), presence (db), dry/wet mix (percent), output gain (db), bypass (toggle).

PLUGIN 2 — plugins/de-esser/de-esser.plugin.json (id 'de-esser', displayName 'De-Esser'). Chain: band-split the sibilant region with g.biquad 'highpass' cutoff = param 'frequency' (~5-9kHz) to isolate sibilants -> envelope-follow that band with g.asymmetricOnePole (attack/release coefs derived from attack/release params and config.sampleRate) on g.abs of the band -> compute reduction: when the envelope exceeds threshold (param 'threshold' db, use g.dbToLin / g.compareLt / g.sub / g.clamp) scale down the sibilant band by 'reduction' amount -> recombine (subtract original band, add ducked band) -> output gain -> tanh safety. Params: input gain (db), frequency (hz), threshold (db), reduction (db or percent), attack (ms), release (ms), output gain (db), bypass (toggle). Dry/wet optional; mixing is via recombination so a dry/wet is not required but a 'reduction'/amount knob is.

PLUGIN 3 — plugins/vintage-lofi-voicer/vintage-lofi-voicer.plugin.json (id 'vintage-lofi-voicer', displayName 'Vintage / Lo-Fi Voicer'). Chain: tilt EQ using two shelving g.biquad stages (lowshelf boost + highshelf cut, single 'tilt' param in db driving both in opposite directions) -> tape-style soft saturation via g.tanh with a 'drive' param scaling input before tanh -> band-limited 'squeeze' via g.biquad 'highpass' (param 'lowCut' hz) then g.biquad 'lowpass' (param 'highCut' hz) -> dry/wet mix (g.lerp) -> output gain -> tanh safety. Params: input gain (db), tilt (db), drive (db or unitless), lowCut (hz), highCut (hz), dry/wet mix (percent), output gain (db), bypass (toggle).

PLUGIN 4 — plugins/digital-degrade/digital-degrade.plugin.json (id 'digital-degrade', displayName 'Digital Degrade / Glitch'). Bitcrush-style corruption approximated with confirmed primitives: quantize amplitude with a staircase built from g.mul (scale up by 2^bits), g.clamp, and reconstructing an integer-like step via g.sub of a fractional part approximated through g.mul/g.clamp arithmetic, then g.div back down — DOCUMENT in the header comment that true rounding/bit-reduction is not in the confirmed primitive set so this is an amplitude-staircase APPROXIMATION. Add distortion drive via g.tanh (param 'drive'), and filtered corruption via g.biquad 'lowpass' (param 'tone' hz). Chain: input gain -> drive (tanh) -> bit-staircase quantize (param 'bits' or 'crush') -> lowpass 'tone' -> dry/wet mix (g.lerp, param 'amount'/'mix' percent) -> output gain -> tanh safety. Params: input gain (db), drive (db/unitless), crush/bits (unitless or percent), tone (hz), dry/wet mix (percent), output gain (db), bypass (toggle).

PLUGIN 5 — plugins/telephone-radio-band/telephone-radio-band.plugin.json (id 'telephone-radio-band', displayName 'Telephone / Radio Band'). Chain: aggressive bandpass via g.biquad 'highpass' cutoff ~300Hz (param 'lowCut' hz, default ~300) then g.biquad 'lowpass' cutoff ~3.4kHz (param 'highCut' hz, default ~3400) -> drive via g.tanh (param 'drive') -> dry/wet mix (g.lerp, param 'mix' percent) -> output gain -> tanh safety. Params: input gain (db), lowCut (hz), highCut (hz), drive (db/unitless), dry/wet mix (percent), output gain (db), bypass (toggle).

PLUGIN 6 — plugins/vocal-drive-edge/vocal-drive-edge.plugin.json (id 'vocal-drive-edge', displayName 'Vocal Drive / Edge'). Soft-to-hard grit. Chain: input gain -> pre-emphasis via g.biquad 'highshelf' or 'highpass' to lift highs before saturation (param 'edge'/'preEmphasis' db) -> soft-to-hard saturation via g.tanh with a 'drive' param, blend soft/hard using g.lerp between a gentle tanh and a harder clamped tanh (param 'hardness' percent) -> dry/wet mix (g.lerp, param 'mix' percent) -> output gain -> tanh safety. Params: input gain (db), edge/preEmphasis (db), drive (db/unitless), hardness (percent), dry/wet mix (percent), output gain (db), bypass (toggle).

UI.COMPACT for each plugin: a grid layout with unit 'gr' containing boxes that position widgets (knob for continuous params, toggle for bypass, optional label boxes) with x/y/w/h coordinates, each referencing its paramName. Keep the grid tidy (e.g. a 2-3 row layout). Mirror the same compact layout inside source.metadata.ui.compact.

After writing all six files, validate every file is parseable JSON by running: python3 -c "import json,glob; [json.load(open(f)) or print('OK', f) for f in sorted(glob.glob('plugins/**/*.plugin.json', recursive=True))]" from the repo root. Fix any JSON errors (embedded JS goes inside a JSON string, so escape quotes/newlines correctly — prefer building the code string carefully; newlines inside the JS may be represented with \n in the JSON string).

Audit primitives: for each plugin, grep the source.code for occurrences of 'g.' and confirm every called method is in the confirmed list. Report any approximations made (expected: the digital-degrade bit-staircase).
acceptance_criteria: Six files exist at plugins/<name>/<name>.plugin.json for the six named plugins.
Running python3 -c "import json,glob; [json.load(open(f)) for f in glob.glob('plugins/**/*.plugin.json', recursive=True)]" exits 0 with no exception (all valid JSON).
Each plugin JSON has top-level id, kind, displayName, description, ports, parameters, source (lang/metadata/code), and ui; structurally parallel across all six.
Every g.* call in every source.code is a member of the confirmed primitive list; no delay/reverb/noise/LFO/oscillator/FFT primitives appear.
Each plugin includes a bypass toggle, input gain, output gain, a tanh output-safety stage, and a dry/wet mix where mixing is meaningful.
Each source.code begins with a header comment describing the signal chain; digital-degrade documents its bitcrush approximation.
verification: python3 -c "import json,glob; files=sorted(glob.glob('plugins/**/*.plugin.json', recursive=True)); [json.load(open(f)) for f in files]; print('valid json:', len(files), 'files')"
grep -o 'g\.[a-zA-Z]*' on each plugin's code and manually confirm membership in the confirmed primitive list
findings: Built all six Tier-1 Suno Studio plugins at plugins/<name>/<name>.plugin.json. JSON validation passes (verification prints 'valid json: 6 files', exit 0). Primitive audit passes: every g.* call across all six source.code strings is in the confirmed set. NOTE: a naive regex 'g\.([a-zA-Z]+)' flags 'sampleRate' as unconfirmed, but that is a false positive from matching the substring inside 'config.sampleRate'; there is no g.sampleRate call. DSP approximations made: (1) digital-degrade bitcrush — a true bit-reduction needs a rounding/floor primitive which is not confirmed, so bit reduction is an AMPLITUDE-STAIRCASE approximation built from g.mul/g.sub/g.clamp/g.div (documented in that plugin's code header). (2) de-esser envelope — g.asymmetricOnePole attack/release coefs are derived as coef = clamp(1 - 1/(seconds*sampleRate), 0, 0.9999) since no exp() primitive is available (a samples-based one-pole approximation). (3) de-esser gating uses g.compareLt(threshold, env) as a hard 0/1 mask scaled by the reduction amount rather than a smooth gain-computer curve. Bypass in every plugin is a g.lerp(bypass, processed, dry) select; every plugin ends with a g.tanh output-safety stage. de-esser intentionally has no dry/wet (mixes via band recombination) and exposes a 'reduction' amount instead, per the spec. Plugins are UNVERIFIED: Node and Suno Studio are not available in this sandbox, so the DSP could not be executed. Per the user instruction, also added plugins/README.md and a CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry documenting that these are Suno Studio effects applied to rendered audio and are NOT lyric tags (fuller docs remain scoped to FEAT-002/FEAT-003).
